title: eval-harness: add prompt-set regression gating with CI hooks and metric thresholds
author: Ava Martinez
ci_checks: benchmarks: warn (1% slowdown on long-context test)
description:
Motivation: We need deterministic CI-level gating for prompt-set regressions so model/service changes cannot silently degrade quality. This PR wires the eval-harness into the main CI pipeline with configurable metric thresholds and per-prompt-set gating. Goals: 1) Run a small, fast subset of evaluation prompt-sets on each PR. 2) Fail CI when a configured metric regresses beyond thresholds for a prompt-set. 3) Surface actionable diffs (per-prompt metrics + examples) in CI artifacts and the PR checks UI.

What this changes: Adds a new evaluation CI job (eval-regression-checks) that runs the lightweight prompt-sets against the candidate model/container. Evaluation config is declarative (eval/config/prompt_gates.yaml) and supports per-prompt-set thresholds, metrics (accuracy, exact_match, rouge-l, embedding-sim), and fallback behavior (block/notify). The job produces both a human-readable HTML report and a machine-readable JSON artifact used by the CI check to decide pass/fail. We also add a small Python runner wrapper (tools/eval/ci_runner.py) used by GitHub Actions to invoke the harness with consistent runtime flags, cache behavior, and output paths.

Developer-facing notes: - Default behavior for new prompt-sets is notify (non-blocking) to avoid accidental CI breakage while ramping. Existing critical prompt-sets are set to block by ENG-3241. - New config includes allowlists for noisy prompts and minimum sample sizes. - There is a feature flag (eval_regression_ci=true) toggled in the Actions workflow to gate rollout.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for the de/serialization and threshold logic are included. Integration flow was validated by executing the new job against a canary model and a set of historical model snapshots to confirm expected pass/fail behavior. CI run summary is attached in artifacts for the merge.

Rollout plan: enable eval_regression_ci for core services first, monitor false positives for 2 weeks in notify mode, then flip to block for high-priority prompt-sets. A follow-up will add per-team override policies and alerting integration with PagerDuty for blocked merges.

Checklist: - [x] Add eval config schema and example prompt_gates.yaml - [x] Implement ci_runner wrapper and GitHub Actions job - [x] Add unit + integration tests - [x] Add HTML + JSON artifacts and CI pass/fail logic - [x] Docs: docs/eval/ci-gating.md (usage + rollout)

Links: Linear ENG-3241, SUP-402 for customer regression reports, docs/eval/ci-gating.md for usage.

review_comments:
Daniel Kim: Can we make the JSON artifact format stable? Unknown fields caused flakiness in the past.

Ava Martinez (author): JSON schema added and validated in unit tests; versioned via top-level 'schema_version'.

Priya Shah: The default notify behavior is sensible, but can we add a per-repo opt-out?

Ava Martinez: Added allowlist config + feature flag; noted opt-out in docs.

Liam O'Connor: Benchmarks show a ~1% slowdown for long-context workloads in the eval runner; it's probably due to extra serialization. Is that acceptable?

Ava Martinez: We implemented streaming JSON to reduce memory churn; follow-up (ENG-3310) will optimize end-to-end. The slowdown is surfaced as a warn in CI but does not block.

Reviews: Daniel Kim approved, Priya Shah approved after minor doc updates, Liam O'Connor requested a follow-up ticket for perf. Merge performed by squash after CI pass.
release_notes: Add CI-level prompt-set regression gating: configurable thresholds, per-prompt-set block/notify modes, and GitHub Actions job producing HTML and JSON artifacts for human and machine consumption. Default rollout is notify for new prompt-sets; critical sets are blocking as configured by ENG-3241.
